Fixed in round 3 (0e220984).

Right. And since round 2 had already fixed this block, the class was named too narrowly: it is not "the export does not persist" but "the install depends on which shell, if any, starts Codex". bash reads `~/.bashrc` in a terminal and `~/.bash_profile` in a macOS login shell, zsh reads `~/.zshrc`, fish needs other syntax, and a session started from an editor may read none of them — so per-shell alternatives would still leave members of that set open.

Fixed in round 5 (05ce0b0c) — declining the suggestion, with the reason now in the docs.

The reading is right that the default path reads `$HOME`; the premise that this is a launcher dependency the router can hit is not. Codex's user scope is `$HOME/.agents/skills` (its skill documentation, cited at `docs/install.md` under "`~/.agents/skills` puts nothing in your repository"), so the discovery that loads the user-scope copy reads the same `$HOME`. A session whose `HOME` is not the one the install ran under never loads this router from there, and one that loads a project copy misses all four resolutions and stops with the router's message rather than guessing (`.agents/skills/revloop/SKILL.md`, "If none resolve, stop"). There is no launch in which the user-scope router runs and its default path points at the wrong home.

Anchoring the route to the installed skill instead would rest on whether Codex hands the router a resolved or a lexical path to its own file, which nobody has measured — the relative fallback it already has is exactly that anchor, and from `~/.agents/skills/revloop/` it resolves to `~/procedures/`.

The paragraph is now in `docs/install.md` and in the router's item 4, so the next reader finds the reason there rather than in this thread.
